objective: Bind every published evaluation aggregate to a bounded per-run evidence index, name the run ids behind each numerator, and publish a deterministic aggregate digest a reviewer can recompute from the referenced runs.
decision_supported: Do the published aggregate metrics describe a named, reproducible set of runs, or is the total separated from the evidence that produced it?
acceptance: Metrics JSON gains a runs array with a bounded per-run run_id, source_class, event_log_sha256, manifest_sha256, final_outcome, evidence_refs and that run's contributions to every aggregate.

metric_contributors names, per aggregate, the run ids that supplied its numerator; a metric with no contributor publishes an explicit empty list and the matching metric_exclusions reason instead of being silently absent.
evidence_index_sha256 is computed over the canonically sorted run records, the contributor sets and the aggregate values, so a reviewer can recompute it.
Reordering the input run files produces the same evidence_index_sha256.
Editing a run id, an event-log hash, a manifest hash, a metric contribution or an aggregate value changes evidence_index_sha256.
The digest excludes run_dir, so the same run set moved to another path keeps its digest.

verify_evidence_index refuses a metrics record whose aggregate differs from its per-run rebuild, whose contributor set its run records do not support, whose run records are not uniquely ordered, or whose digest does not match its content; collect() calls it before returning.
Every aggregate metric is rebuildable from runs[] alone, and a metric with no declared zero-contributor value fails closed rather than publishing an invented number.
A run present in the run directory that cannot contribute to a metric is reported in metric_exclusions with a reason, not dropped.
A nonzero recovery_rate names at least one run whose contributions carry the recovery numerator, with its log and manifest hash.
generate_report.py refuses to render a report from metrics without a rebuildable index, and shows a bounded run count plus the digest prefix per column rather than the run list.

compare_evaluations.py carries each version's evidence_index digest, its VTCR contributor run ids, evidence_indexes_match and every_version_has_an_evidence_index, without changing its Wilson or difference intervals.
Existing eligibility and percentile calculations keep their current fail-closed behavior; no metric definition, threshold or reader schema changes.

evidence: Focused unit output for the evidence index: per-aggregate contributor sets, permuted-input digest vectors, edited-run-id/log-hash/manifest-hash/contribution/aggregate digest vectors, an explicit zero-contributor aggregate, and the refused drifted-index, stale-digest and indexless cases.

A run-to-metric attribution table emitted by collect() for a grasp-failure fixture, showing recovery_rate 1.0 against the run id whose contributions carry numerator 1 and whose event_log_sha256 and manifest_sha256 are both populated.
Report output showing a bounded run count, the digest prefix and the evidence-index reference instead of the full run list, plus the refusal of an indexless metrics file.

stop_conditions: An interfaces/ or libs/contracts/ schema, Pydantic model or reader-contract change is required rather than an additive metrics field.
The design would expose raw evidence payloads, camera frames or private participant data; only reference strings may leave the run directory.
A published aggregate metric cannot be rebuilt from a per-run contribution without changing that metric's definition, threshold or fail-closed behavior.
A downstream consumer outside tools/scripts/generate_report.py, tools/scripts/compare_evaluations.py and tools/scripts/check_evaluation_eligibility.py would break on the added metrics field.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, or an allowed path contains unrelated user modifications.
data_classification: Local deterministic JSON event fixtures and hashes only; no personal data, no camera content and no network access.
model_policy: Reuse the existing release_eligibility hashing and predicate helpers; no evaluation-owned hash algorithm, no new dependency and no metric-definition change.
risks_and_fallbacks: collect_metrics.py computes each aggregate twice: once from the events and once from its own per-run contributions. verify_evidence_index refuses the record when the two disagree, so the duplication is a cross-check rather than two definitions that can drift.

The digest excludes run_dir because it is a local path, not evidence. The consequence is that two collections of the same run set in different directories share a digest by design; the run_dir label beside it still says which directory was read.

MAX_INDEXED_RUNS is 256. A larger collection is refused rather than truncated, because a partial index cannot cover the run set it claims to explain; raising the bound is a later change if a real collection exceeds it.

false_completion_count and recovery_rate publish null rather than 0 when no run could contribute. That preserves the existing not-reviewed and no-recoverable-run behavior; the change is that the run ids behind the null are now named.

compare_evaluations.compare still accepts an indexless metrics dict so the existing percentile tests keep testing percentile math, but its main() refuses to publish a comparison built from one, and the output records every_version_has_an_evidence_index false.
Rollback is reverting this commit: the index and digest fields are additive, and no consumer stores or migrates a metrics record it cannot regenerate.
